details.title: Arban – Chromatic Scale No. 1
details.lead: From Arban's Grande méthode complète de cornet à pistons et de saxhorn, first edition, 1864. The notes are the cornet part as printed, in written pitch for the B♭ cornet. Below: the book's own words, translated from the French.
facts: Arban, Grande méthode complète de cornet à pistons et de saxhorn, first edition (Paris: Léon Escudier, 1864)

sections.heading: Chromatic scales and triplets
paragraphs: The chromatic scale is among the most essential, and I have given it a great deal of room. This kind of study makes the fingering easy. Take care to press the valves all the way down, so that every note comes out full.

Work slowly at first, making the rhythms shown clearly heard. In this scale, as in the diatonic scales, swell the sound going up and lessen it coming down. Above all, play strictly in time, without hurrying the end of each phrase as many artists are in the habit of doing. So I advise using the metronome, to reach the exactness that makes playing beautiful.

sources.title: IMSLP: Grande méthode complète de cornet à pistons (Arban), first edition, Paris 1864
